sources.title: Guidelines to the Practice of Anesthesia—Revised Edition 2026
reviewed_propositions: Airway plans distinguish face-mask, supraglottic, and tracheal-airway techniques and require equipment for oxygenation and ventilation.
Tracheal intubation provides a cuffed airway when aspiration protection and controlled ventilation are required.

sources.title: Practice Guidelines for Management of the Difficult Airway
reviewed_propositions: Face-mask ventilation, supraglottic airways, tracheal intubation, and invasive airways are distinct airway-management techniques.
An invasive airway is reserved for a cannot-intubate/cannot-oxygenate pathway rather than routine initial aspiration protection.

sources.title: Evaluation and management of enuresis in the general paediatric setting
reviewed_propositions: Monosymptomatic enuresis has no daytime lower urinary tract symptoms; nonmonosymptomatic enuresis does.
Primary enuresis means the child has never achieved at least six months of dryness; secondary enuresis follows a dry interval.
Diabetes and urinary infection are uncommon but important alternative causes when their clinical features are present.

sources.organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
sources.title: Bedwetting in under 19s: recommendations
reviewed_propositions: Assessment asks about daytime urinary symptoms, previous dryness, fluid intake, comorbidity, and features suggesting diabetes or urinary infection.
Urinalysis is targeted to recent onset, daytime symptoms, illness, suspected urinary infection, or suspected diabetes.

sources.organization: Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada
sources.title: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Position Statement
reviewed_propositions: PCOS is considered with ovulatory dysfunction and clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism after excluding important mimics.
Marked androgen excess or virilization warrants evaluation for an androgen-secreting disorder.

sources.title: Recommendations from the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for PCOS
reviewed_propositions: Evaluation for PCOS excludes thyroid disease, hyperprolactinemia, and nonclassic congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
Hypothalamic amenorrhea and androgen-secreting tumours are distinguished using the clinical pattern and targeted testing.

sources.organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
sources.title: Surgical site infections: prevention and treatment
reviewed_propositions: Postoperative wound pain, erythema, local inflammatory signs, and purulent drainage support surgical-site infection.
Other postoperative sources of fever require assessment when the wound does not localize the infection.

sources.organization: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.title: NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual: Surgical Site Infection Event
reviewed_propositions: Purulent drainage from an incision is a defining criterion used in surgical-site infection surveillance.
An infection is assigned to the surgical site rather than another source when the operative incision meets the relevant criteria.

sources.organization: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health
sources.title: Psychosis: Diagnosis
reviewed_propositions: Psychotic presentations require assessment of delusions, hallucinations, disorganization, mood episodes, substance exposure, duration, and functional change.
Preserved function outside a persistent delusional belief and absence of broader schizophrenia features support delusional disorder.

sources.organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
sources.title: Psychosis and schizophrenia in adults: recommendations
reviewed_propositions: Assessment of psychosis includes psychiatric symptoms, medical history, prescribed and non-prescribed drugs, and occupational and social function.
Mood, substance-related, and schizophrenia-spectrum explanations must be assessed rather than inferred from delusions alone.

sources.title: COVID-19 pandemic guidance for the health care sector
reviewed_propositions: Scarce-resource allocation should use a fair, transparent, uniform, evidence-based, and objective process.
Triage should optimize resource use while protecting dignity and avoiding arbitrary differences between patient groups.

sources.title: Public health ethics framework for response to the COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
reviewed_propositions: Allocation choices should be justified through proportionality, equity, reciprocity, and respect for persons and communities.
Social worth, socioeconomic status, and similar personal characteristics do not determine inherent worth.

question.stem: During a regional emergency, two patients need the only immediately available ICU bed. A pre-established triage process estimates that one patient has substantially greater urgent clinical need and a substantially higher likelihood of short-term benefit. Both patients have equal legal status and neither has prior claim to the bed.
question.lead_in: Which allocation approach is most appropriate?
options: Prioritize clinical need and expected benefit using the transparent triage process
Use a random lottery despite the prognostic difference
Prioritize the patient with greater perceived social worth
Prioritize the patient able to pay privately
question.answer: Prioritize clinical need and expected benefit using the transparent triage process
question.reason: A transparent, consistently applied process may use objective clinical need and expected benefit. Arrival order or lottery can be tie-breakers only in narrower equal-claim settings; social worth and ability to pay are inequitable criteria.
